The probability of each specific sequence of 2 heads and 1 tail is \(\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3\), since each flip is independent and has a probability of \(\frac{1}{2}\) of landing heads.

The binomial coefficient \(\binom{3}{2}\) is calculated as follows:
\[
\binom{3}{2} = \frac{3!}{2!1!} = 3
\]

\[
P(\text{exactly 2 heads}) = \binom{3}{2} \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3 = 3 \left(\frac{1}{8}\right) = \frac{3}{8}
\]

\[

\]

\[
\left| P(\text{exactly 2 heads}) - P(\text{3 heads}) \right| = \left| \frac{3}{8} - \frac{1}{8} \right| = \left| \frac{2}{8} \right| = \frac{1}{4}
\]

Therefore, the positive difference between the probability of a fair coin landing heads up exactly 2 times out of 3 flips and the probability of a fair coin landing heads up 3 times out of 3 flips is \(\boxed{\frac{1}{4}}\).
